title: Newton's First Law
learning_goal: Explain equilibrium and inertia using Newton's First Law.

stages.title: 1. Newton's First Law
stages.content: An object remains at rest or continues moving at constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force. This tendency to resist a change in motion is called inertia.

stages.title: 2. Inertia and mass
stages.content: Mass is a measure of inertia. An object with greater mass is harder to speed up, slow down, or redirect than an object with less mass.

stages.title: 3. Equilibrium
stages.content: When the net force on an object is zero, the object is in equilibrium. It may be at rest or moving at constant velocity.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A book rests on a table. Gravity pulls downward while the table's normal force pushes upward with equal magnitude. The net force is zero, so the book remains at rest.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A hockey puck slides across nearly frictionless ice at constant velocity. What does Newton's First Law tell you about the net force on the puck?
stages.hint: Constant velocity means the motion is not changing.
stages.alternate_explanation: If the puck is neither speeding up, slowing down, nor turning, its acceleration is zero. Zero acceleration means the forces are balanced.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, identify examples of inertia, distinguish balanced from unbalanced forces, explain equilibrium, and predict motion when the net force is zero.
